script: Work is found in four main places. Online freelance marketplaces connect you with clients all over the world. Direct clients are people you find yourself, such as a local shop, a clinic, a school or a restaurant. Community groups on Facebook and WhatsApp often post small digital jobs. And remote employers hire part-time staff for support, data and content work. Set your expectations for the first year. Your first jobs will be small, and they may pay less than you hope. This is normal. Their real purpose is to give you experience and reviews. Clients rarely hire someone with no reviews, so your first two or three jobs are about building trust, not about big money. Here is a simple example. Imagine a woman at her kitchen table who writes a short description for a bakery's new menu. The bakery pays her a fixed amount for that task. That is project pay. Next month, the same bakery asks her to send twenty product descriptions, one at a time, and pays for each one.
